title: Digital research collection highlights Pauling celebration
notes: Confirms 46 research notebooks, 1922-1994, about 7,500 pages, containing calculations, experimental data, conclusions and future research ideas. Use as archive map, not as primary evidence for a specific decision.

title: The Structure of Proteins: Two Hydrogen-Bonded Helical Configurations of the Polypeptide Chain
notes: Primary publication inspected through CaltechAUTHORS. The paper explicitly states that the group accumulated accurate crystal-structure information on amino acids/peptides to obtain interatomic distances, bond angles and configurational parameters, then used those constraints to construct hydrogen-bonded helices.

title: Linus Pauling Oral History Interview
stable_locator: Caltech Oral Histories, interview 10 May 1984; resolver CaltechOH:OH_Pauling_L
notes: First-person retrospective evidence. Pauling reflects on the alpha helix, including that he believed he could have found it earlier if he had concentrated enough effort on the problem. Retrospective testimony is not treated as contemporaneous evidence.

title: The Alpha Helix
notes: Archive-based reconstruction: in March 1948 Pauling drew correct bond angles/distances on paper, folded the chain, and explored hydrogen bonding. It also records the 5.4 A model versus Astbury's 5.1 A repeat discrepancy and the later synthetic-polypeptide evidence that reduced the force of that constraint. Use as archival synthesis, not as a substitute for the original 1948 object.

title: Linus Pauling and the Structure of Proteins: A Documentary History
notes: Documentary-history gateway with letters, manuscripts, papers, photographs and AV material. Individual contemporaneous primary records still need direct inspection before the alpha episode can be upgraded to high confidence.

title: Sickle Cell Anemia, a Molecular Disease
stable_locator: Science 110(2865):543-548; DOI 10.1126/science.110.2865.543; Gates and Crellin contribution 1333
notes: Primary team-authored publication. Caltech metadata confirms the four authors and identifies physicians who supplied blood samples. Do not attribute the experimental program solely to Pauling.

title: Harvey A. Itano, Research Report for Admission to Candidacy
stable_locator: Ava Helen and Linus Pauling Papers, I: Individual Correspondence, Harvey A. Itano; Research Report for Admission to Candidacy, April 1948, p.10
notes: Primary-process document identified through archival scholarship but not yet directly opened in this build. Secondary transcription reports that Itano proposed a complete electrophoretic study of normal hemoglobin as a comparison basis for sickle-cell hemoglobin. Do not quote as DIRECT_EVIDENCE until the archival object is inspected.

title: It's in the Blood: The Varieties of Linus Pauling's Work on Hemoglobin and Sickle Cell Anemia
stable_locator: OSU M.S. thesis, Chapter 2; discussion of Itano electrophoresis work and archival footnotes around pp. 64-66 of the PDF text extraction
notes: Archive-based secondary reconstruction. It identifies the Itano research report, Itano dissertation, and Pauling-Burch correspondence as underlying primary records, and describes Singer/Itano electrophoresis work in summer 1948.

title: A Proposed Structure for the Nucleic Acids
notes: Primary publication inspected through indexed full-text copies. The paper calls the model promising and precisely specified, while explicitly stating that detailed intensity calculations had not yet been made and that the structure could not be considered proved correct.

title: The Pauling-Corey Structure of DNA
notes: Archive-based reconstruction of the late-1952 modeling process. It records limited X-ray evidence, severe core-packing difficulty, Corey's calculations showing insufficient room, and Pauling/Corey's decision to submit on 31 December 1952 despite acknowledged model tightness and incomplete fit.

title: Linus Pauling's manuscript describing incorrect triple helix — Peter Pauling interview
authors: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory DNA Learning Center
notes: Participant retrospective account. Peter Pauling recalls that Linus lacked good information on DNA water content and diameter and later characterized the acid-state mistake as simply an error. Use as retrospective calibration, not contemporaneous proof of motive.

title: Linus Pauling and the Race for DNA: A Documentary History
notes: Gateway to original letters, lab notes, photographs and manuscripts. Direct primary objects must be separately registered.
